Concrete defects & structural safety10 questions+
  1. Is honeycombing in concrete dangerous?
    Published answer

    Honeycombing is a voided or stony area where mortar has not properly filled around the coarse aggregate. It can be superficial, but deep honeycombing may reduce effective concrete section, expose reinforcement and allow water and chlorides to reach the steel. Do not decide safety from appearance alone. Photograph the area, record its location and extent, avoid covering it with plaster, and ask the structural engineer to inspect, sound and assess the concrete. Where needed, the engineer may specify cover removal, reinforcement checks, testing and an engineered repair. Active cracking, exposed or corroded bars, or honeycombing at a column joint or beam-column zone needs prompt assessment.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
  2. What causes honeycombing in concrete columns?
    Published answer

    Common causes include inadequate vibration or compaction, congested reinforcement that blocks concrete flow, a mix that is too harsh or poorly proportioned, excessive free fall or segregation, leaking formwork joints, and placing concrete in lifts without proper consolidation. A column cage with closely spaced bars, laps or embedded services is particularly difficult to fill. Prevention starts before pouring: check bar spacing and cover, seal the shuttering, confirm the approved mix and workability, plan the pour sequence and access for the vibrator, and use trained workers. Adding water at site to make concrete flow is not a safe substitute for a properly designed workable mix.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – concrete standards directory ↗
  3. How do you repair honeycomb in an RCC column?
    Published answer

    There is no safe one-method repair for every honeycombed column. First have the structural engineer map the defect, determine its depth and whether reinforcement is exposed, loose or corroded, and assess whether the member has lost section or bond. The repair specification may require removal of unsound concrete to a sound substrate, cleaning and treatment of reinforcement, reinstatement with an approved repair mortar or micro-concrete, and curing. Deep defects may need designed form-and-pour repair or strengthening. Do not simply fill the surface with plaster, cement slurry or putty. Keep records and obtain the engineer’s inspection and acceptance before concealing the repair.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  4. Can a honeycombed column be repaired?
    Published answer

    Many honeycombed columns can be repaired, but repairability depends on defect depth, affected area, reinforcement condition, load stage and the column’s structural demand. A shallow surface void may need a different treatment from a deep void that exposes bars or interrupts the concrete core. Stop finishing work over the defect and request an on-site assessment by the structural designer. The engineer may call for measurements, sounding, cover checks or appropriate non-destructive/destructive tests before choosing a repair or strengthening design. Do not load or alter the member based on a contractor’s visual assurance alone.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  5. Are cracks in a newly constructed house normal?
    Published answer

    Some fine cracks can occur as plaster, mortar or concrete dries and shrinks, but a new house should not be assumed safe or defective from the word “crack” alone. Note the crack’s width, length, direction, location and whether it changes over time; photograph it with a scale and date. Hairline plaster cracks differ from diagonal cracks through masonry, cracks in beams or columns, widening cracks, displacement, water ingress or doors suddenly jamming. Report defects to the builder in writing and ask the structural engineer to assess any structural-looking or progressive crack. Do not hide cracks with putty before the cause is understood.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗BIS – standards portal ↗
  6. Which wall cracks are dangerous in a house?
    Published answer

    Warning signs include cracks that keep widening, pass through masonry rather than only paint or plaster, run diagonally from door or window corners, appear with wall bulging or separation, occur alongside sagging floors or beams, or are accompanied by settlement and water damage. A single crack width does not reliably classify safety: material, location, movement and structural system matter. Photograph and monitor the crack without delaying professional review if it is growing or associated with distortion. Keep people away from visibly unstable areas and have a qualified structural engineer inspect before carrying out cosmetic repairs.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  7. Why are diagonal cracks appearing near doors and windows?
    Published answer

    Door and window corners are stress-concentration points, so diagonal cracks can arise from shrinkage, poor masonry bonding, inadequate or poorly supported lintels, differential movement, settlement or detailing problems where masonry meets an RCC frame. Check whether the crack is limited to plaster or continues through the wall, whether it appears on both sides, and whether it is widening. Photograph it and review the lintel, bearing, wall junction and foundation movement with the project engineer. Do not assume that adding mesh or filler is enough until the cause is identified.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  8. What is the minimum concrete cover for RCC columns and slabs?
    Published answer

    There is no single cover value that homeowners should apply to every column or slab. Required nominal cover depends on the structural member, exposure condition, fire-resistance requirement, concrete and reinforcement details, and the applicable design standard. The approved structural drawings should state the specified cover; verify it before concrete is poured using suitable cover blocks or spacers and an inspection record. Do not reduce cover to make reinforcement fit, and do not use broken brick pieces as substitutes. If the drawing is silent or site conditions differ, ask the structural designer to issue a written clarification.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  9. How long should a newly cast roof slab be cured?
    Published answer

    Curing duration must follow the concrete specification, cement type, weather and the engineer’s instructions; a fixed number copied from another project is not a substitute. The goal is to keep the concrete sufficiently moist and protect it from rapid drying, especially during Hyderabad’s hot and windy periods. Start curing as soon as the surface can be treated without damage, use ponding or another approved method, prevent water from escaping and keep a daily site record. Do not remove formwork or props just because the surface looks hard; removal and reshoring must follow the structural engineer’s sequence and strength requirements.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  10. How can I check concrete quality before slab casting?
    Published answer

    Before the pour, compare the latest structural drawing and bar-bending schedule with the installed reinforcement. Check bar diameter, spacing, laps, anchorage, cover blocks, chairs, beam-column joints, shuttering line and level, tight joints, props, openings, sleeves, electrical conduits and plumbing embeds. Confirm concrete grade, approved mix or supplier, delivery/testing plan, access, vibrator availability, pour sequence and curing arrangements. Ask the engineer or authorised supervisor to sign a pre-pour checklist and photograph concealed work. Once concrete is placed, many of these items cannot be checked without intrusive work.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – concrete mix proportioning IS 10262 ↗
Cement, steel & construction materials10 questions+
  1. Which cement is best for house construction in India?
    Published answer

    There is no universally best cement brand or type for every part of a house. The structural designer and project specification should select a conforming cement type based on the concrete or masonry application, exposure, strength development, heat and construction method. Compare the applicable BIS standard and valid product marking, manufacturer traceability, batch and packing date, intact bags and storage condition. Buy from an authorised supplier, keep bags dry and raised off the floor, and use older stock first. Do not select cement only by advertising or switch type mid-project without the engineer’s approval.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗BIS – cement and concrete standards ↗
  2. Which is better for house construction: OPC or PPC cement?
    Published answer

    OPC and PPC are both used in construction, but they behave differently and are not interchangeable in every specification. OPC is often selected where earlier strength development or a specified construction sequence is important; PPC contains pozzolanic material and can offer durability and lower heat benefits when properly specified and cured, while its early strength development may differ. The right choice depends on the structural mix design, exposure, placing schedule and curing plan. Follow the engineer’s specification and the cement’s applicable BIS standard rather than choosing by a blanket “stronger” claim.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗BIS – cement and concrete standards ↗
  3. Which TMT steel is best for house construction?
    Published answer

    Choose reinforcement steel by the grade and ductility required in the structural drawings, not by brand popularity alone. Check the manufacturer’s identification rolled on the bar, invoice and batch traceability, applicable BIS licence/marking, test certificate and consistency of bar diameter and condition. Ask the engineer to approve any proposed brand or grade substitution before purchase or installation. Do not accept badly rusted, oily, bent or untraceable bars without assessment. Steel grade, ductility, bend performance and detailing all matter; a higher number on the label is not automatically a safer choice.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗BIS – steel and concrete standards ↗
  4. What is the difference between Fe 500 and Fe 500D steel?
    Published answer

    The grade designation describes specified mechanical properties; the “D” suffix in Fe 500D denotes higher ductility requirements than ordinary Fe 500 under the relevant reinforcement standard. Ductility is important because reinforcement should be capable of deformation before fracture, particularly under dynamic or seismic demands. The exact grade must still match the structural designer’s drawings and applicable standard. Check the current BIS specification and test certificate for the supplied batch. Do not assume that Fe 500D can automatically replace every grade or that grade alone compensates for poor detailing and workmanship.

    Official referencesBIS – steel standards and grade lookup ↗
  5. Is Fe 550 steel better than Fe 500D for a house?
    Published answer

    Not automatically. Fe 550 has a higher specified yield strength, but a higher strength grade does not by itself make a residential structure safer or more economical. Ductility, elongation, bend performance, seismic detailing, bar congestion, anchorage and the design assumptions all matter. A structural engineer may specify a particular grade for a reason; changing it can affect reinforcement quantities and detailing. Never substitute Fe 550 for Fe 500D—or the reverse—without written approval and confirmation that the design and code requirements remain satisfied.

    Official referencesBIS – steel standards and grade lookup ↗
  6. How do I identify original TMT steel?
    Published answer

    Inspect the raised or rolled identification on the bar for the manufacturer and grade markings, and match them with the supplier invoice, bundle tags and batch test certificate. Confirm the product’s applicable BIS licence and marking through BIS resources; do not rely only on a printed sticker or QR code supplied by a seller. Check diameter and surface condition at delivery, keep material segregated by grade and batch, and retain a sample or records if the engineer requires testing. If markings are missing, inconsistent or suspicious, quarantine the batch and ask the engineer and supplier to resolve it before use.

    Official referencesBIS – product and licence lookup ↗
  7. Which is better: red bricks or AAC blocks?
    Published answer

    Neither is best for every wall. Red clay bricks and AAC blocks differ in weight, dimensions, thermal behaviour, sound performance, water absorption, fixing requirements and workmanship. AAC is lighter and can reduce dead load, but needs compatible mortar, careful handling, correct anchors and manufacturer-recommended finishing. Brickwork may suit local availability and familiar workmanship, but quality and dimensions vary. Compare tested product properties, wall thickness, structural loads, plaster system, service chasing and total installed cost. Confirm the selected masonry system with the architect and structural engineer before changing the drawings.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
  8. Is M-sand better than river sand for house construction?
    Published answer

    Manufactured sand can be a suitable alternative to natural river sand when it is produced, graded and tested to the applicable specification. The important checks are grading, fines and dust content, particle shape, cleanliness, source consistency and suitability for the intended concrete or mortar. Concrete sand and plastering sand may need different grading characteristics. Ask for test results and have the mix designed or approved for the actual material; do not judge by colour or price alone. A change in sand source can change water demand and workability, so inform the engineer before use.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 383 aggregate standard ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
  9. Which aggregate size is used for roof slab concrete?
    Published answer

    Aggregate size is selected by the concrete mix designer with regard to slab thickness, clear spacing between reinforcement, cover, placing method and the member geometry. The largest nominal size must be small enough to pass through the reinforcement and compact without segregation or honeycombing. A generic “20 mm for every slab” rule can be unsuitable in congested or thin sections. Confirm the approved mix design and aggregate grading with the structural engineer or ready-mix supplier, and do not change aggregate size at site without approval.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 383 aggregate standard ↗BIS – IS 10262 concrete mix proportioning ↗
  10. How can I check cement quality before buying?
    Published answer

    Check that each bag is sealed, dry and undamaged, with a readable manufacturer name, cement type, applicable standard marking, batch/packing details and traceable invoice. Avoid bags that are lumpy, damp, torn or stored directly on a wet floor or exposed to rain. Confirm the supplier is authorised and verify product claims through BIS resources where applicable. Visual checks cannot establish cement strength or genuineness conclusively; if a batch is doubtful, hold it and arrange appropriate testing rather than using it in structural concrete.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗
House construction cost & budgets10 questions+
  1. What is the house construction cost per square foot in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    There is no dependable single per-square-foot rate for every Hyderabad house. A meaningful estimate needs the plot and site conditions, total built-up area, number of floors, structural system, finish level, service scope, access and the contractor’s inclusions. Ask for a BOQ that separates structure, masonry, plaster, waterproofing, electrical, plumbing, doors/windows, flooring, painting, approvals, taxes and external works. Confirm whether the rate is based on built-up or carpet area and whether GST, borewell, compound wall, lift, modular kitchen and interiors are excluded. Compare like-for-like written specifications, not headline rates.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approvals and project documentation ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  2. How much does it cost to build a 2BHK house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    A 2BHK label alone is not enough to price a house. First establish the sanctioned buildable area, room sizes, floor count, parking and stair arrangement. Then specify the structural grade, wall system, electrical and plumbing points, windows, doors, tiles, sanitaryware, kitchen scope, painting and external works. Obtain an itemised BOQ with quantities, unit rates, exclusions, taxes and payment stages. Ask contractors to price the same drawings and material schedule. Treat online totals as early budgeting guides only; a measured site visit and design are needed for a project estimate.

    Official referencesBuildNow – Telangana building approval portal ↗
  3. How much does it cost to build a 3BHK house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    The cost of a 3BHK depends mainly on total permitted built-up area and specification, not simply the number of bedrooms. A larger living/dining area, additional bathrooms, balconies, staircase, parking, premium windows, electrical loads and kitchen/wardrobe scope can materially change the total. Ask for a room-wise scope and detailed BOQ, identify provisional allowances and exclusions, and compare the same drawings across contractors. Keep a separately identified contingency for unknown site conditions and owner-selected upgrades; do not treat a generic online figure as a quotation.

    Official referencesBuildNow – Telangana building approval portal ↗
  4. How much does it cost to build a 100 square yard house?
    Published answer

    A 100-square-yard plot is 900 square feet of land, not necessarily the permitted built-up area. The actual house size depends on jurisdiction, road width, setbacks, parking, height, land use and sanctioned floor configuration. Confirm the legal buildable envelope first, then calculate total floor area and prepare a BOQ for structure, masonry, services and finishes. Include approval costs and site-specific items such as excavation, retaining work, drainage or utility connections where applicable. Never estimate from plot area alone.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗BuildNow – current rules and orders ↗
  5. What is the construction cost for a 30x40 house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    A 30x40 plot has 1,200 square feet of plot area, but setbacks, parking and other approval conditions determine how much can be built. Decide the permitted floor plan and total built-up area before estimating. Prepare a BOQ covering foundation, RCC, masonry, plaster, waterproofing, doors/windows, electrical, plumbing, flooring, painting and external works. State whether compound wall, sump, overhead tank, borewell, lift, kitchen and wardrobes are included. Compare quotations on identical drawings and specifications rather than using a fixed plot-size price.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  6. How much does a G+1 house construction cost?
    Published answer

    For a G+1 estimate, calculate the total built-up area of both floors and confirm that the plot can legally accommodate the proposed height, setbacks and parking. Foundation and structural design must account for the intended total building, even if the upper floor is constructed later. Separate costs for foundation, frame, slabs, walls, stairs, services and finishes, and clarify whether the roof terrace, parapet, water tanks and future-floor provisions are included. Ask for a stage-wise BOQ and engineer-approved drawings before accepting a lump sum.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approvals ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  7. What is included in a house construction package?
    Published answer

    A construction package may include only labour, labour plus selected materials, or a turnkey scope. Never assume the label defines the work. Request a written schedule for design and approvals, excavation, foundation, RCC, masonry, plaster, waterproofing, electrical, plumbing, doors/windows, flooring, painting, fixtures, external development, testing and handover. For every item specify brand or performance grade, quantity, finish, exclusions, taxes and who supplies it. Clarify whether compound wall, borewell, sump, septic/sewer connection, lift, modular kitchen, wardrobes and landscaping are included.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval checklist ↗
  8. How do I calculate the built-up area of a house?
    Published answer

    Built-up area is generally measured using the covered constructed area at each floor, including wall thickness and certain covered spaces as defined by the measurement convention used in the contract or approval. Carpet area is the usable internal floor area; plot area is the land parcel. These are not interchangeable. Ask the architect and contractor to state the exact measurement method, floor-wise dimensions and treatment of balconies, staircases, shafts and service areas. Use the sanctioned drawings and contract definition when comparing rates so that the same area basis is used.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  9. How much does a house construction contractor charge?
    Published answer

    Contractors may quote a labour-only rate, labour plus materials, item-rate BOQ or turnkey lump sum. The amount varies with design, site access, project size, specification, supervision, risk allocation and inclusions. Ask what the fee covers: labour, procurement, tools, scaffolding, wastage, transport, testing, site management, taxes and defect rectification. Request references and a sample BOQ, then compare the total cost and exclusions. Avoid paying a large advance without a written contract and measurable milestones.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  10. How much extra budget should I keep for unexpected construction costs?
    Published answer

    Set a project contingency based on design maturity, site uncertainty and how much work remains undefined; there is no universal percentage that fits every project. Early estimates with incomplete drawings need more allowance than a fully surveyed, designed and itemised project. Keep contingency separate from known upgrades and taxes. Track committed cost, approved variations, pending selections and paid invoices in one budget. Do not spend the contingency on cosmetic upgrades before excavation and concealed services are complete.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval checklist ↗
Contractors & construction companies10 questions+
  1. What are the top 10 construction companies in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    A ranked “top 10” list would be misleading unless the ranking method, project evidence and date are published. Instead, shortlist companies whose completed work matches your building type, budget and location. Verify the legal entity, visit active and completed sites, speak with recent clients, inspect workmanship after monsoon, compare itemised BOQs and confirm who supervises the work. Check approval responsibilities, written specifications, milestone payments, defect response and dispute terms. Treat paid listings and social-media popularity as advertising, not proof of quality.

    Official referencesMCA – company/LLP master data ↗BuildNow – Telangana approval portal ↗
  2. Which is the best house construction company in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    There is no single best company for every project. The right contractor is one with verifiable experience in a similar house, transparent scope and pricing, qualified design and site supervision, documented quality checks and a reliable defect-response process. Visit completed projects, contact owners independently, compare the same drawings and BOQ across bidders, and verify the contracting legal entity. Ask who is accountable for approvals, structural design, materials, safety, delays and handover. Choose on evidence and contract clarity rather than a generic ranking.

    Official referencesMCA – company/LLP master data ↗BuildNow – Telangana approval portal ↗
  3. How do I choose a reliable house construction contractor?
    Published answer

    Shortlist contractors whose experience matches your project type, scale and finish level. Visit at least one active site and completed home, speak privately with past clients, verify the business identity and check who will supervise daily work. Ask for itemised specifications, drawings, a realistic schedule, quality inspection points, payment milestones, variation rates, insurance and written defect-liability terms. Make payments against measured progress and documented approvals rather than large advances. Keep an independent architect or engineer involved for design review and quality checks; a polished brochure is not evidence of workmanship.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  4. What questions should I ask a construction company before signing?
    Published answer

    Ask who prepares and owns the drawings; who obtains approvals; what exact materials, grades, brands and quantities are included; what is excluded; how area is measured; who supervises and signs off concealed work; how quality tests are recorded; what the schedule and delay remedies are; how price escalation and variations are approved; how payments are linked to milestones; who handles utilities and debris; what insurance and safety arrangements exist; and how defects are reported after handover. Get every answer, drawing, specification and commercial promise attached to the signed agreement.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval checklist ↗BIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  5. How can I verify a construction company in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Verify the legal business name, registration details where applicable, GST details if represented as registered, physical office, authorised signatory and the entity that will sign your contract and issue invoices. Visit active and completed projects, speak to previous clients, inspect workmanship and ask who supervises the site daily. Check whether professional designers and engineers are named and whether required approvals are being obtained. Search for complaints and litigation where appropriate, but assess evidence carefully. Do not rely solely on social-media followers, testimonials or a website portfolio.

    Official referencesMCA – company/LLP master data ↗GST – taxpayer search ↗
  6. Is turnkey house construction better than hiring separate contractors?
    Published answer

    Turnkey construction can simplify coordination because one contractor manages multiple trades, but the owner depends heavily on the clarity of the scope, quality controls and contract. Separate contractors can provide more direct control over brands and pricing, but the owner or project manager must coordinate sequence, interfaces, delays and defects. Compare total cost, responsibility for design coordination, procurement, site supervision, testing, safety and warranties. Choose based on your time, technical oversight and risk tolerance, and keep an independent professional to review quality.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  7. What should a house construction agreement include?
    Published answer

    A useful construction agreement identifies the parties and site, attaches approved drawings and a detailed BOQ/specification, defines inclusions and exclusions, sets the contract price and tax treatment, and states how measurements and variations are valued. It should also cover milestones and payment evidence, start and completion dates, extension-of-time events, quality inspections and testing, safety and insurance, material substitutions, site records, defect-liability and warranty procedures, handover documents, termination, dispute resolution and governing law. Have a lawyer review the contract and ensure verbal promises are written into its schedules before signing.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  8. How do I compare two house construction quotations?
    Published answer

    Put both quotations into the same comparison sheet and align the scope before comparing totals. Check built-up area and measurement method; drawings; concrete grade and mix; steel grade; block/brick type; plaster and waterproofing systems; electrical and plumbing brands; flooring and sanitaryware allowances; labour, transport, taxes and approvals; supervision; testing; timeline; exclusions; escalation; variation rates; payment milestones and defect-liability terms. Ask each contractor to price missing items and clarify provisional sums in writing. The lowest headline rate may exclude major work, so compare the final like-for-like scope and contract risk.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approvals and documents ↗BIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  9. How do I check the quality of a builder's completed projects?
    Published answer

    Visit more than one completed home and, if possible, an active site. Look beyond decorative finishes: inspect terrace and bathroom leakage history, external-wall dampness, door and window operation, tile lippage, drainage falls, electrical labelling, plumbing access and visible cracks. Ask owners about delays, variations, after-sales response and defects that appeared after monsoon. Request permission to review sanctioned drawings and handover documents. A short walkthrough cannot certify structural safety, so use an independent engineer for technical concerns.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  10. What is the difference between a builder, contractor and construction company?
    Published answer

    A builder may develop or sell a property and can carry responsibility for land, approvals and delivery; a contractor is typically engaged to execute defined construction work; a construction company may provide contracting, project management or turnkey services. These labels are not a substitute for reading the contract. Identify who owns the land, who obtains approvals, who designs, who employs subcontractors, who invoices, who supervises and who is liable for defects. Ensure the exact legal entity and scope are written into the agreement.

    Official referencesMCA – company/LLP master data ↗
House plans, plots & permissions10 questions+
  1. What documents should I check before buying a plot in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Before paying an advance, ask an independent property lawyer to examine the original registered sale deed and the link documents that establish the seller’s title. Match the seller, survey number, subdivision, plot number, extent and four boundaries across the documents and the physical site. Obtain an Encumbrance Certificate for an appropriate period and check registered-document details, but do not treat an EC as conclusive proof of clear title: it may not reveal every dispute, unregistered claim or boundary problem. Check the approved layout and its conditions with the competent authority, permitted land use in the applicable master plan, conversion status where relevant, legal road access, road-widening reservations, acquisition or prohibited-property issues, and any lake, nala or other buffer restrictions. Compare revenue/land records and survey maps with a licensed surveyor’s site measurement. Check tax dues, mortgages and release documents, seller identity and authority to sell. For a plotted development, verify TGRERA registration where the project is required to be registered. Do not rely on a broker’s brochure, a neighbour’s documents or a bank’s loan approval instead of independent legal and survey checks.

    Official referencesBhu Bharati – land details ↗Bhu Bharati – registered document details ↗Telangana RERA – project search and citizen information ↗
  2. How do I get building permission in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Start by confirming the exact survey number, village/local-body jurisdiction, land use and whether the plot is in an approved layout. As of November 2026, Telangana’s official BuildNow portal is the current unified online entry point for building and layout approvals; its notice says the older TG-bPASS portal was to close after 15 December 2025. Engage a licensed architect or other authorised technical professional to prepare the site information, drawings and required design documents. The BuildNow checklist identifies ownership documents (sale deed and link documents) and a front-side site photograph as core uploads; depending on the case, it can also require layout approval, property-tax or VLT receipts, a market-value certificate, earlier building approval or other supporting documents. Larger, taller, non-residential or otherwise sensitive proposals may need the single-window process and departmental NOCs. Follow the route shown for your actual plot and building category, pay the assessed fees, respond to scrutiny comments and download the final digitally issued proceedings and sanctioned plan. An application receipt or payment confirmation is not the building permit.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official Telangana approval portal ↗BuildNow – document checklist ↗BuildNow – government orders and amendments ↗
  3. What is the difference between GHMC and HMDA approval?
    Published answer

    GHMC and HMDA have different roles; they are not interchangeable labels for the same approval. GHMC is a municipal corporation responsible for local civic administration and functions within its notified limits. HMDA is the metropolitan planning and development authority, dealing with the wider metropolitan planning framework and matters such as master-plan land use and layouts within its jurisdiction. A property may therefore need a planning/layout or land-use check as well as a building-plan sanction from the authority or local body that has the relevant power. The responsible authority can depend on the exact village, survey number, land type and the latest government delegation of powers. Hyderabad’s urban and municipal boundaries and delegations have changed, including government orders issued in 2026, so do not decide jurisdiction from a postal address or an old GHMC/HMDA label. Check the current BuildNow workflow and confirm the competent authority for the property. An HMDA layout approval by itself is not the same thing as approval of your individual house plan.

    Official referencesBuildNow – integrated approval portal and departments ↗BuildNow – current government orders and jurisdiction-related amendments ↗HMDA – planning department ↗
  4. How much setback is required for a house in Telangana?
    Published answer

    There is no single setback distance that applies to every house in Telangana. The required open space depends on the plot’s dimensions and area, the width of the abutting road, the proposed building height and use, the number of floors, the plot shape and whether it is a corner site or faces more than one road. The calculation may also be affected by road-widening lines, master-plan reservations, lake/nala Full Tank Level or buffer restrictions and other site-specific conditions. The applicable Telangana Building Rules and later government amendments must be checked for the proposal being submitted; the rules and portal workflows can change. Ask a licensed architect to survey the plot, confirm the jurisdiction and run the current BuildNow scrutiny against the proposed drawings before you finalise a floor plan. Do not copy a neighbour’s setback or rely on a generic online table: even nearby plots can have different road widths, dimensions, reservations or approval conditions.

    Official referencesBuildNow – government orders and current rule amendments ↗BuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  5. Can I build a house without building permission in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Do not start construction on the assumption that permission is unnecessary. Building without a required sanction or registration can lead to enforcement action, including demolition of unlawful work, and can create problems with utilities, sale, finance and future approvals. There are narrow category-based exceptions: BuildNow’s current FAQ says an individual residential plot up to 75 square yards with ground or ground-plus-one construction follows an online registration route rather than a normal building-permission approval. That is not a blanket exemption for larger plots, additional floors, other building uses or sites affected by special restrictions; the required online registration and all applicable conditions still matter. Check the current BuildNow FAQ and have a licensed technical professional verify your plot, proposed height, land use and jurisdiction before work begins. Do not treat an application number, fee receipt, unapproved layout, verbal assurance or a neighbour’s unauthorised building as permission. If construction has already started, get professional advice on the actual status and lawful next steps; regularisation should never be assumed.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official FAQs, including small-plot registration and enforcement ↗India Code – Telangana State Building Permission Approval and Self Certification System Act, 2020 ↗BuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  6. What is an occupancy certificate and is it required for a house?
    Published answer

    An Occupancy Certificate (OC) is an official record issued after completion checks where required. It confirms that the completed building has met the applicable approval conditions sufficiently for occupation; it is different from the original building permission and from a private handover or possession letter. Whether an OC is required depends on the building category, plot area, height and current rules. BuildNow’s published FAQ says an individual residential building on a plot up to 200 square metres with a height up to 7 metres is exempt from applying for an OC; other categories may require an OC through the portal. Do not apply that threshold to every residential, apartment, high-rise or non-residential project. Check the current BuildNow rules for the specific sanctioned plan, complete any required inspections and retain the final OC or applicable exemption/registration records. When buying a completed property, compare the actual building with the sanctioned plan and verify the OC where the rules require one.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official FAQs on occupancy certificates ↗BuildNow – occupancy certificate process and timelines ↗
  7. Which direction is best for a house entrance?
    Published answer

    There is no one entrance direction that is best for every plot or that guarantees a better home. First consider where the road and legal access are, the shape and slope of the site, room arrangement, privacy, daylight, heat gain, prevailing breezes and practical vehicle or pedestrian entry. A well-designed entrance should work with the overall circulation and should not force poor ventilation, awkward rooms or unsafe structural changes. Your architect can study the site orientation and sun path, then use window placement, shading, verandas and landscaping to manage daylight and heat. If Vastu is important to your family, share those preferences at the start so they can be considered alongside structural design, ventilation, safety and approval rules. Treat Vastu direction as a personal or traditional preference, not as a substitute for building regulations or technical planning.

  8. How do I plan a 30x40 house floor plan?
    Published answer

    A 30x40 plot is 1,200 square feet of plot area, not automatically 1,200 square feet of permissible built-up area. Start with a measured survey, road side and width, north direction, local jurisdiction, setbacks, parking and any reservations. Then prepare a room schedule for bedrooms, bathrooms, kitchen, living, stair and storage, and test circulation, daylight, cross-ventilation and privacy. Have the architect check the current BuildNow rules before fixing the layout, and have the structural engineer coordinate the column grid and future floors. Do not copy a plan from another 30x40 plot without checking its site and approval conditions.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official Telangana approvals ↗BuildNow – current rules and government orders ↗
  9. How many floors can I build on a 100 square yard plot?
    Published answer

    Plot area alone cannot determine the permitted number of floors. The answer depends on the exact plot dimensions, abutting road width, land use, approved layout, jurisdiction, setbacks, building height, parking, fire and other applicable rules, plus structural capacity. A 100-square-yard plot in one locality may have different constraints from a similar plot elsewhere. Have a licensed architect verify the survey number and current BuildNow scrutiny route, then obtain a written feasibility plan before buying or designing. A contractor’s promise or a neighbouring building is not proof of permission.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official Telangana approvals ↗BuildNow – FAQs ↗
  10. Should I get a soil test before building a house?
    Published answer

    A geotechnical investigation is the reliable way to understand the ground conditions that influence foundation design. It can identify soil layers, groundwater level and engineering parameters needed by the structural/geotechnical designer. The number and depth of boreholes depend on the plot, building loads, ground variability and professional scope; do not choose them from a generic internet rule. A soil report helps the engineer select and design an appropriate foundation and reduces the risk of differential settlement or costly redesign. Avoid deciding footing size or foundation type solely from a nearby plot or a contractor’s thumb rule.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
Waterproofing, dampness & roof leakage10 questions+
  1. Why is my newly built house wall getting damp?
    Published answer

    Dampness can come from plumbing leaks, failed bathroom or terrace waterproofing, rain entering through cracks and joints, ground moisture rising through walls, poor drainage or condensation. Map where and when it appears: after rain, after bathing, near pipes, at the wall base or on cold surfaces. Check the other side of the wall and nearby floors/terraces. Ask a plumber or building-envelope specialist to test the likely source before replastering or repainting. A waterproof coating on the visible patch may only hide the symptom.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  2. How do I stop terrace leakage permanently?
    Published answer

    A durable terrace-leakage repair begins by locating the water path, not by applying another coat over the visible stain. Inspect slab cracks, parapet junctions, pipe penetrations, door thresholds, rainwater outlets, slope and ponding. Remove failed layers as specified, repair the substrate, form proper coves and upturns, install a compatible waterproofing system with correct thickness and detailing, and protect it with the specified finish. Test the completed system before covering it and keep outlets clear. If leakage is coming from plumbing or a crack caused by movement, membrane coating alone will not solve it.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  3. What is the best waterproofing for a bathroom?
    Published answer

    The best system is the one compatible with the substrate, water exposure, drain detail, tile finish and manufacturer’s installation requirements. A complete wet-area system treats the floor, wall-floor junctions, corners, pipe penetrations, thresholds and drain flange as one continuous detail. The substrate must be sound and correctly sloped; apply the specified primer and membrane thickness, reinforce corners where required, allow curing, and carry out a documented water test before tiling. Do not rely on tile grout or a surface sealant as the primary waterproofing layer.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  4. Why is water leaking from the bathroom ceiling?
    Published answer

    A bathroom ceiling leak may come from a failed floor waterproofing layer, a leaking concealed supply or waste pipe, a drain connection, a shower enclosure detail or water entering from another nearby area. First identify whether the leak occurs only when a fixture is used, after bathing, or during rain. Avoid breaking the ceiling at random: have a plumber isolate and pressure-test supply lines and inspect drainage, while a waterproofing specialist checks the wet-area membrane and junctions. Repair the source, test it, dry affected materials and then reinstate the ceiling finish.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  5. How do I fix seepage on an external wall?
    Published answer

    Inspect the full external elevation for open cracks, failed sealant, parapet and coping joints, window perimeters, AC pipe penetrations, balconies and roof junctions. Check whether water is entering from a plumbing line or from rain exposure. Repair the source and substrate first, then use a compatible crack-repair, joint-sealant or facade-waterproofing system specified for the material and exposure. Prepare the surface and allow correct curing; painting over damp masonry traps the problem. For recurring or widespread seepage, obtain a specialist inspection and written method statement.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  6. Is waterproofing required before laying bathroom tiles?
    Published answer

    A properly designed wet-area waterproofing system is a key part of preventing water from reaching the slab and adjacent rooms. Tiles and grout are not themselves a reliable waterproof barrier. Before tiling, check that the substrate is prepared, floor falls lead to the drain, corners and wall-floor junctions are detailed, pipe penetrations are sealed, the membrane is continuous and cured, and the specified water test has passed. Keep photographs and test records. The system and upturn height should follow the project specification and manufacturer’s technical instructions.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  7. How do I prevent water leakage from a balcony?
    Published answer

    Balcony leakage usually relates to poor slope, blocked or undersized outlets, failed waterproofing, cracks, inadequate upturns or water passing at the door threshold and railing fixings. Confirm that water flows to the drain without ponding and that the waterproofing layer is continuous at corners, walls and penetrations. Test the system before installing or reinstating tiles. Keep drain grates clear and inspect sealant joints periodically. If water has already entered the slab or room below, identify and repair the cause before replacing ceiling finishes.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  8. What causes white salt deposits on house walls?
    Published answer

    White powdery deposits are often efflorescence: soluble salts move with moisture through masonry or plaster and crystallise as water evaporates. The deposit itself is a symptom, not the moisture source. Check for rising damp, leaks, rain penetration, wet construction materials or poor drainage. Dry brushing may remove loose salts after the area dries, but do not seal or repaint until the moisture path is addressed and the surface is suitable for the specified finish. Persistent or heavy deposits need a building professional to investigate the source.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  9. How often should terrace waterproofing be renewed?
    Published answer

    There is no fixed renewal interval for every terrace. Service life depends on the waterproofing system, substrate movement, UV and weather exposure, protective screed or tiles, drainage, workmanship and maintenance. Inspect after monsoon and whenever ponding, blistering, open joints or ceiling dampness appears. Follow the manufacturer’s maintenance schedule and keep installation and test records. Renew or repair based on condition and system requirements, not simply by applying a new coating every few years over an unknown or failing layer.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  10. How can I reduce roof heat in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Start by checking roof exposure, existing waterproofing, ventilation and whether the terrace can support the proposed treatment. Options include a compatible high-reflectance roof coating, insulation below or above the slab, shaded terrace structures, pergolas or solar panels with appropriate clearances. Each option has different cost, maintenance, waterproofing and structural implications. Do not cover drains or trap water beneath a new layer. Ask the architect or specialist to coordinate thermal performance with waterproofing, roof slope, access and structural loading.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code and building services ↗
Electrical, plumbing & home systems10 questions+
  1. Which wire is best for house wiring in India?
    Published answer

    Select wires by conductor material and cross-section, insulation type and temperature rating, circuit load, installation method and applicable Indian standards—not by brand name alone. A qualified electrical designer should calculate loads and circuit sizes for lighting, sockets, ACs, geysers, kitchen appliances and other high-demand equipment. Check manufacturer traceability, relevant BIS marking/licence where applicable, genuine sealed packaging and compatible conduits and accessories. Provide proper earthing, circuit protection and testing. Never increase a breaker rating to stop tripping without checking the cable and circuit design.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  2. How many electrical points are needed in a 2BHK house?
    Published answer

    There is no fixed point count for every 2BHK. Prepare a room-wise schedule based on furniture, appliance locations and how the family uses each space. Include general sockets, dedicated circuits for ACs, geysers and kitchen appliances, refrigerator, washing machine, exhaust fans, internet/router, TV, lighting, outdoor points and future provisions. Coordinate switch heights and socket positions with wardrobes, beds and kitchen modules before conduit work. Have a qualified electrician size circuits, protection and earthing, then test and label the distribution board.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
  3. What is the best location for a water tank in a house?
    Published answer

    Tank location must be coordinated with structural capacity, plumbing head, access for cleaning, overflow and drain routing, hygiene and visual impact. An overhead tank adds a significant concentrated load, so the structural engineer must design the supporting slab, beams or platform for the filled tank and maintenance access. A ground-level or underground tank needs safe access, protection from contamination and suitable pump arrangements. Keep tanks away from sewage contamination risks and provide screened vents, covers and overflow discharge to a safe drain.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  4. How do I calculate overhead water tank capacity for a house?
    Published answer

    Estimate daily demand from the number of occupants, usage pattern, local supply reliability and any applicable water-supply design criteria. Separate drinking and domestic use if different sources are used, and consider whether the tank is intended for one day or a shorter backup period. Size the tank with the plumber/engineer, check the supporting structure for the full water load, and provide a float valve, overflow, drain, access cover and cleaning access. Do not choose capacity only from a neighbour’s tank size.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  5. What is the difference between CPVC and UPVC pipes?
    Published answer

    CPVC is commonly used for hot and cold pressurised water distribution within its rated temperature and pressure range. uPVC is commonly used for cold-water, soil, waste and drainage applications depending on the product series and standard. The correct choice depends on the service, operating temperature, pressure, jointing system and manufacturer’s rating. Do not mix incompatible fittings or adhesives. Ask the plumber to specify the pipe standard, pressure class, diameter and intended use, and pressure-test concealed lines before closing walls.

    Official referencesBIS – Know Your Standard ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  6. Why is water pressure low on the top floor?
    Published answer

    Low pressure at the top floor can result from insufficient tank head, undersized or long pipe runs, partially closed valves, clogged filters, air locks, leaks or a pump/pressure-system fault. Check whether the problem affects every tap or only one fixture and whether it occurs at particular times. Have a plumber inspect valves, filters, pipe sizing and pump controls. If a booster pump is needed, size it for the building and provide suitable pressure control and dry-run protection; do not install an oversized pump without checking the system.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  7. How do I plan electrical wiring before plastering?
    Published answer

    Freeze the furniture and appliance layout first, then prepare a room-wise point schedule, circuit plan and distribution-board schedule. Mark switchboards, sockets, AC and geyser points, kitchen loads, data/TV points, lighting, outdoor fittings and future provisions on the drawings. Coordinate conduit routes with beams, columns, plumbing and false ceilings; avoid cutting structural members. Check conduit continuity, box alignment, wire draw paths and earthing before plastering. Photograph concealed routes and have a qualified electrician inspect and test the installation before energising.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
  8. Is solar power worth installing for an independent house?
    Published answer

    Solar can be worthwhile when roof area, shade, household consumption, daytime usage, grid connection and available incentives align. Review at least 12 months of electricity bills, check usable unshaded roof area and structural condition, and ask an authorised installer to size the system against actual consumption. Compare equipment warranties, inverter replacement assumptions, generation estimates, net-metering/export rules and maintenance. Confirm the current Telangana DISCOM and national scheme process before paying an installer; incentives and approvals can change. Keep access to drains and roof waterproofing in the design.

    Official referencesPM Surya Ghar – official rooftop solar scheme ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  9. What is rainwater harvesting and is it compulsory in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Rainwater harvesting collects roof or site runoff and directs it through filters to storage or recharge structures. Whether a particular system is mandatory, and what design applies, depends on the property type, plot and current local rules. Check the sanctioned plan and the competent authority’s current conditions rather than relying on a generic claim. A good system includes clean roof catchments, first-flush diversion where specified, suitable filtration, safe overflow, access for maintenance and protection against contamination. Do not direct runoff into a neighbour’s property or a sewer connection without approval.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official Telangana approval portal ↗HMDA – planning information ↗
  10. How do I prevent plumbing leakage inside walls?
    Published answer

    Use a coordinated plumbing layout with accessible valves, correctly rated pipes and fittings, compatible jointing materials and minimal concealed joints. Have the installer follow the manufacturer’s method, support pipes properly and protect them from damage during later trades. Pressure-test supply lines and test drainage before plastering or tiling; record the test results and photograph pipe routes. Avoid burying service joints where access is impossible. If leakage occurs, isolate the line and locate the source before opening walls or applying surface sealants.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗BIS – Know Your Standard ↗
Home buying, maintenance & contractor decisions10 questions+
  1. What should I inspect before taking handover of a new house?
    Published answer

    Carry out a room-by-room snag inspection before final payment and possession. Check visible cracks and dampness; terrace and bathroom water tests; roof and balcony drainage; doors, windows, locks and glass; tile levels and hollow-sounding areas; paint finish; electrical switches, sockets, earthing and distribution-board labels; water pressure, hot-water points, traps and leaks; sanitary fixtures; stair and railing safety; parking and external drainage. Collect sanctioned plans, completion/occupancy documents where applicable, warranties, test reports, equipment manuals, keys, meter details and a signed list of defects with closure dates. Use an independent professional for structural or technical concerns.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official Telangana approval and OC process ↗BuildNow – OC timelines ↗
  2. How do I check whether a house is structurally safe?
    Published answer

    A visual walkthrough cannot certify structural safety. Look for progressive cracks, settlement, tilted or bulging walls, sagging beams or slabs, exposed/corroded reinforcement, water-damaged structural members and doors/windows suddenly binding, but absence of visible signs is not proof of safety. Obtain the approved structural drawings, soil report and alteration history where available. Have a qualified structural engineer inspect the building and decide whether measurements or tests are needed. Do not remove walls, cut structural members or add floors without a designed assessment.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗BIS – reinforced concrete standards ↗
  3. What is a snag list in house construction?
    Published answer

    A snag list is a written record of incomplete work, defects and items that must be corrected before handover or final closure. Organise it room by room and include a photo, exact location, description, responsible party, agreed correction and target date. Check finishes, doors, windows, plumbing, electrical, drainage, waterproofing and supplied equipment. Separate cosmetic snags from safety or technical concerns that need specialist inspection. Reinspect each item after correction and record closure; do not rely on verbal assurances.

    Official referencesBuildNow – occupancy and handover process ↗
  4. How long does it take to construct a 2BHK house?
    Published answer

    Construction duration depends on approvals, design readiness, built-up area, number of floors, foundation conditions, procurement, labour availability, weather, inspection hold points and how quickly the owner makes decisions. A realistic programme should show design and approvals, site preparation, foundation, structure, masonry, services, finishes, testing and handover as separate activities. Ask the contractor for a baseline schedule with dependencies and milestone dates, then update it weekly. Avoid promises based only on a generic number of months without a site survey and defined scope.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval service timelines ↗
  5. What is the correct order of house construction work?
    Published answer

    A typical sequence is site survey and investigation, design and approvals, setting out, excavation and foundations, plinth and ground preparation, columns/beams/slabs, masonry, concealed electrical and plumbing, plastering, waterproofing and testing, flooring and wall finishes, doors/windows, fixtures, painting, external works, commissioning and handover. The exact sequence changes with the design and construction method. Coordinate every concealed service before closing walls or slabs, and do not proceed past structural or waterproofing inspection hold points without sign-off.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval process ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  6. How often should a house be painted?
    Published answer

    Repainting frequency depends on the paint system, surface preparation, exposure, workmanship, ventilation and maintenance. Exterior walls exposed to strong sun and monsoon may weather faster than protected interiors; damp or salt-contaminated walls should not simply be repainted. Inspect for chalking, peeling, cracks, algae and moisture, then fix the underlying cause, prepare the substrate and use a compatible primer and finish. Follow the manufacturer’s maintenance guidance and keep product details for future touch-ups.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  7. How do I identify poor workmanship in a new house?
    Published answer

    Look for uneven floors, tile lippage, hollow-sounding tiles, inconsistent grout, doors that do not close, leaking traps, low water pressure, unsealed penetrations, poor drainage falls, paint blistering, damp patches, exposed wiring, missing labels and visible cracks. Inspect concealed work before it is covered, because many defects cannot be judged after handover. Record issues with photographs and locations, compare work against drawings and specifications, and ask the relevant professional to assess structural, electrical or plumbing safety concerns.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  8. What maintenance should I do before monsoon?
    Published answer

    Before monsoon, clear terrace and balcony drains, inspect roof slopes and ponding, check parapet and window sealant joints, repair external cracks, inspect downpipes and rainwater outlets, and confirm that site grading carries water away from the foundation. Check sump covers, pump operation and electrical protection in wet areas. Do not climb onto unsafe roofs or work near live electrical equipment. Photograph defects and arrange repairs before heavy rain; repeated leakage should be diagnosed rather than covered with a temporary coat.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  9. How do I reduce construction delays?
    Published answer

    The strongest delay controls are design freeze, early approvals, a realistic procurement schedule and timely owner decisions. Before work starts, complete coordinated architectural and structural drawings, confirm long-lead items, identify utility dependencies and agree inspection hold points. Use a weekly programme showing planned versus actual progress, labour, materials, pending approvals, decisions and blockers. Record changes and their time impact in writing. Avoid starting a trade before preceding work is ready, because rework and site congestion often create more delay than the original task.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval timelines ↗
  10. What warranty should a construction company provide?
    Published answer

    There is no one warranty wording that covers every construction project. The agreement should distinguish workmanship defect liability from manufacturer warranties for products such as pumps, fixtures, appliances, waterproofing systems and equipment. State the start date, duration, covered items, exclusions, reporting method, inspection and repair response times, emergency contact and whether the warranty transfers to a future owner. Keep invoices, product serial numbers, test reports and handover records. Have the contract reviewed so that promises are specific and enforceable under the applicable law.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
Construction estimates & execution12 questions+
  1. How much does foundation work cost for a house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Foundation cost cannot be estimated reliably from plot size alone. It depends on soil profile and groundwater, building loads, foundation type, excavation depth, access, dewatering, disposal, concrete and reinforcement quantities, retaining requirements and site constraints. Obtain a geotechnical investigation and structural design, then price the actual footing or raft drawings through a measured BOQ. Clarify whether excavation, PCC, anti-termite treatment, backfilling, plinth beams, waterproofing and disposal are included. Avoid choosing a foundation type or rate from a neighbour’s project.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  2. What is the cost of RCC slab construction?
    Published answer

    An RCC slab estimate should be built from the approved structural drawings and quantities for concrete, reinforcement, formwork, props, pumping, labour, placing, vibration, testing and curing. Slab thickness, spans, beams, openings, reinforcement, access and floor height change the quantity and method. Ask whether the quoted rate includes steel cutting/bending, shuttering removal, reshoring and test records. Do not use a generic per-square-foot figure as a substitute for the engineer’s design and a measured BOQ.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – concrete mix proportioning ↗
  3. How much does plastering cost per square foot in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Plastering cost depends on internal versus external area, wall height, thickness, surface condition, mortar specification, scaffolding, corner beads, mesh details, curing and finish quality. Confirm whether measurement is by square foot or square metre, how openings are deducted, and whether materials, transport and scaffolding are included. Specify the required line, level, plumb and finish, and inspect sample work before large areas proceed. A rate without thickness and surface-preparation scope is not comparable.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  4. How much does brickwork cost for a house?
    Published answer

    Brickwork cost depends on wall thickness, brick or block type and quality, mortar, wall height, openings, lintels, scaffolding, labour and how quantities are measured. Ask the contractor to state the unit, wall type, material specification, wastage allowance and whether lintels, mesh at junctions and scaffolding are included. Check that the chosen wall system matches the architectural and structural drawings. Compare a measured BOQ rather than a single rate that mixes different wall thicknesses and materials.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  5. How do I estimate steel quantity for house construction?
    Published answer

    The reliable steel quantity comes from structural drawings and the bar bending schedule (BBS), which lists bar diameter, shape, length, bends, laps and quantities for each member. A generic kilogram-per-square-foot thumb rule can be misleading because spans, loads, foundation type, seismic detailing and architectural layout change reinforcement. Ask the engineer or detailer to issue a BBS and reconcile delivered, cut, installed and scrap quantities by floor and member. Do not reduce reinforcement to meet a budget without a redesigned and approved solution.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 1786 reinforcement steel lookup ↗BIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  6. How do I calculate concrete quantity for a house?
    Published answer

    Calculate concrete volume member by member from the approved dimensions: footing, pedestal, column, beam, slab, staircase and other concrete elements. For a simple rectangular element, volume is length × width × depth in metres, giving cubic metres; avoid double-counting intersections between beams, slabs and columns. Use the structural drawings and approved measurement rules, then add only the justified ordering allowance for site conditions and supplier practice. The mix grade and quantity should be checked by the engineer or quantity surveyor before ordering.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – IS 10262 mix proportioning ↗
  7. What is included in a semi-finished house construction package?
    Published answer

    “Semi-finished” is not a standard scope definition, so ask the contractor to list exactly what is complete at handover. It may stop at structure and plaster, or include concealed services, flooring, doors, windows, basic electrical and plumbing, depending on the company. Specify whether painting, sanitary fixtures, switches, kitchen, wardrobes, railings, compound wall, external paving, utility connections, approvals and cleaning are included. Attach a room-wise finish schedule and a signed exclusion list to the agreement.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval checklist ↗
  8. How do I check a construction BOQ before signing?
    Published answer

    Check that every BOQ line has a clear description, unit, quantity, rate, amount and material or workmanship specification. Reconcile quantities with the drawings and confirm how hidden work, openings, wastage, transport, taxes, testing and provisional sums are treated. Look for missing items such as waterproofing, scaffolding, curing, debris removal, utility connections and external works. Ensure brand substitutions and quantity changes require written approval, and that the BOQ is attached to the contract with a clear variation process.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval checklist ↗
  9. Should I pay a construction contractor by stage or monthly?
    Published answer

    Milestone-based payments tied to measurable completed work and inspection sign-off generally give an owner clearer control than paying only by calendar month. A contract can also include periodic measured bills for labour or item-rate work. Define each milestone, evidence required, who certifies it, retention if agreed, treatment of materials stored on site and deductions for incomplete or defective work. Avoid large advances without security and do not pay for concealed work until it has been inspected and recorded.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval and document records ↗
  10. What is a quality checklist before roof slab concrete?
    Published answer

    Before the slab pour, verify the latest drawings, reinforcement diameter and spacing, laps and anchorage, cover blocks, chairs, beam-column joints, slab openings, sleeves, conduits, formwork dimensions and tightness, props and access. Confirm concrete grade and approved mix, delivery and testing arrangements, vibrator and backup equipment, pour sequence, weather plan and curing method. The engineer or authorised supervisor should sign the pre-pour checklist and record photos. Correct defects before concrete arrives; they are difficult to fix after casting.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  11. How do I check waterproofing before bathroom tiling?
    Published answer

    Inspect the waterproofing substrate, slope, drain flange, wall-floor junctions, corners, pipe penetrations and membrane continuity before tiles cover the work. Confirm the specified primer, number of coats or membrane thickness, upturn details and curing time against the manufacturer’s method statement. Carry out and record the specified pond or water test, check the ceiling or adjacent rooms below, and repair any loss before tiling. Photograph the completed system and keep product batch and installer details for future maintenance.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  12. What should I check in a house construction quotation in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Check the plot and jurisdiction assumptions, sanctioned built-up area, floor count, drawings, BOQ quantities, concrete and steel grades, wall materials, waterproofing, electrical and plumbing scope, finish brands, taxes, approvals, site supervision, testing, debris removal, timeline and defect liability. Confirm local site costs such as access, soil, drainage, water and power arrangements. List exclusions such as compound wall, sump, borewell, lift, kitchen, wardrobes and external works. Compare quotations only after each contractor prices the same drawings and specifications.

    Official referencesBuildNow – approval checklist ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
Hyderabad locality project planning4 questions+

    Start with a legal and technical check of the exact plot, not just the locality name. Verify title, survey boundaries, approved layout, land use, road access, reservations and any lake/nala or other buffer restrictions. Confirm the competent authority and current BuildNow route for the survey number. Arrange a site survey and soil investigation, check utilities and ground levels, and prepare a design that respects setbacks, parking, heat and ventilation. Locality-wide assumptions cannot replace plot-specific legal, planning and engineering review.
