  2. What should I check before constructing a house in Tellapur?
    Published answer

    Verify the plot’s registered title, survey number, layout approval and land-use status, then confirm which authority handles the building proposal for that exact village and survey number. Check access road, road-widening reservations, drainage, water and power connections, ground levels and any water-body restrictions. Commission a measured survey and soil investigation before foundation design. Ask the architect to confirm the current BuildNow workflow and permitted building envelope rather than relying on a nearby property’s sanction.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗Bhu Bharati – land status ↗HMDA – planning ↗
  3. What affects house construction cost in Miyapur?
    Published answer

    The largest cost drivers are total permitted built-up area, number of floors, foundation and soil conditions, structural design, material specification, finish level, service requirements and site access. Existing structures, narrow approach roads, debris removal, utility connections and drainage can also affect the estimate. Ask contractors to inspect the actual site and price a common BOQ with the same exclusions and taxes. Avoid treating a locality label as a fixed rate; two plots in Miyapur can have very different conditions and scopes.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  4. How do I plan a house construction project in Kondapur?
    Published answer

    Begin with title and layout verification, a measured site survey, soil investigation and confirmation of the competent approval authority for the exact plot. Freeze the room brief and coordinated architectural/structural/service drawings before procurement. Confirm the BuildNow application route, approvals and utility dependencies, then select a contractor using a comparable BOQ and written milestones. Track procurement, site inspections, variations, safety and progress weekly. Check access, drainage and neighbouring conditions during the site visit rather than assuming all plots in the locality are alike.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗Bhu Bharati – land status ↗
Planning, room sizes & building services20 questions+
  1. What is the ideal column spacing for a residential house?
    Published answer

    There is no universal ideal column spacing. The structural grid depends on room layout, spans, loads, number of floors, soil and foundation conditions, concrete and steel grades, architectural openings and seismic design requirements. Large spans can increase beam depth and cost; adding columns without coordination can obstruct rooms and parking. Have the architect and structural engineer coordinate the grid early and issue calculations and drawings. Never shift, remove or resize a column on site to solve a layout problem without a redesigned and approved structural solution.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗BIS – reinforced concrete standards ↗
  2. What is the ideal ceiling height for a house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Choose ceiling height by balancing comfortable clear headroom, local approval rules, room proportions, ventilation, heat, false-ceiling services, fan clearance and construction cost. Distinguish floor-to-floor height from the finished clear height after slab, flooring and ceiling finishes. Check the applicable building rules and the architect’s coordinated sections before fixing the level. Do not copy a neighbour’s measurement without checking the building category, services and sanctioned drawings.

    Official referencesBuildNow – current rules and orders ↗BIS – National Building Code ↗
  3. How much parking space is needed for a 30x40 house?
    Published answer

    Parking must be planned around the actual vehicle dimensions, turning path, gate width, column locations, pedestrian access and whether a second vehicle or two-wheeler must fit. On a 30x40 plot, setbacks and the permitted building envelope may limit the usable parking footprint. Draw the vehicle swept path and check that doors can open without blocking the entrance or staircase. Confirm the parking requirement and layout through the current local approval rules before finalising the plan.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗
  4. How do I plan natural ventilation in a house?
    Published answer

    Plan ventilation with the site orientation, prevailing wind, neighbouring buildings, room use, privacy and window locations in mind. Cross-ventilation works best when there are appropriately placed openings that allow air to enter and leave, rather than windows on one wall only. Provide exhaust ventilation for kitchens and bathrooms where needed, and coordinate window sizes with daylight, heat gain, noise, security and structure. An architect should assess the actual site; adding windows later may conflict with privacy, fire, structural or approval constraints.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  5. How many bathrooms should a 2BHK house have?
    Published answer

    A 2BHK can work with one shared bathroom or with one shared plus one attached bathroom; the right choice depends on household size, guests, privacy, budget and available floor area. Plan bathroom access from bedrooms and common areas, ventilation or exhaust, waterproofing, floor slope, plumbing shafts and future maintenance. Avoid placing a bathroom door directly into a kitchen or dining space where possible. Ask the architect to coordinate fixture clearances and plumbing routes before fixing room dimensions.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  6. What is the difference between carpet area and built-up area?
    Published answer

    Carpet area refers broadly to the usable floor area within the home, while built-up area generally includes the carpet area plus wall thickness and certain covered spaces. Plot area is the land area and is different again. Exact definitions can vary by the context, agreement and applicable regulation, so ask for a dimensioned area statement that identifies balconies, shafts, stairs and common areas separately. When a contractor quotes a per-square-foot rate, make sure the rate and measured area use the same stated basis.

    Official referencesRERA – Telangana official portal ↗
  7. How much does house painting cost in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Painting cost depends on wall and ceiling area, surface condition, putty and primer requirements, number of coats, interior or exterior exposure, paint type, colour changes, scaffolding and labour. Ask for a measured area statement and a written brand/product schedule with preparation steps, coat count and finish. Clarify whether crack filling, damp treatment, sanding, masking and cleanup are included. Compare sample panels and inspect preparation before the final coats; a low rate may omit essential surface preparation.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  8. How much does electrical wiring cost for a 2BHK house?
    Published answer

    Electrical wiring cost depends on the number and type of points, circuit layout, load and appliance requirements, wire sizes, conduits, switchgear, distribution board, earthing, protection devices, labour and brand specification. Prepare a room-wise point schedule and single-line/circuit plan before requesting quotes. Confirm whether fans, lights, fixtures, data points, AC points, geysers, inverter/solar provisions and testing are included. Have a qualified electrician design and test the installation; do not select cable size by price or copy another home’s layout.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code and electrical services ↗
  9. How much does plumbing work cost for a new house?
    Published answer

    Plumbing cost depends on bathroom and kitchen count, hot-water lines, pipe material and diameter, tank and pump arrangement, drainage routes, shafts, fixtures, concealed versus exposed work and pressure testing. Ask for a fixture and point schedule, pipe brand/specification, valve and access details, drainage slope, testing procedure and inclusions. Clarify whether sanitaryware, taps, pumps, tanks, rainwater lines and external connections are included. Test concealed supply lines and drainage before closing walls and floors, and keep an as-built layout for maintenance.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  10. What is the cost of compound wall construction in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Compound-wall cost depends on boundary length, wall height and thickness, foundation and soil, retaining requirements, columns, coping, plaster and paint, gate openings, security details and site access. First verify the legal plot boundaries with a surveyor and check any road-widening or setback restrictions before building. Ask for separate quantities for excavation, footing, columns, masonry, reinforcement, plaster, coping and gate work. A wall retaining higher ground needs an engineered retaining design, not an ordinary boundary-wall detail.

    Official referencesBhu Bharati – land status ↗BuildNow – official approvals ↗
  11. How much does staircase construction cost for a house?
    Published answer

    Staircase cost depends on floor height, width, number and shape of flights, landing size, RCC or steel construction, support arrangement, finish, railing, headroom and whether it is inside or outside. The structural engineer must design the stair and its supports as part of the building frame. Ask the BOQ to separate concrete, reinforcement, shuttering, steps/finish, railing and lighting. Check comfortable riser and tread proportions, handrail safety and clear headroom against the approved architectural drawings and applicable rules.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  12. What is the best flooring for a new house?
    Published answer

    The best flooring depends on room use, budget, slip resistance, maintenance, wear, water exposure and the quality of installation. Vitrified tiles are common for living spaces; anti-skid finishes may be appropriate for wet areas; natural stone, engineered surfaces and wood-based products have different sealing and maintenance needs. Compare the full installed system, including substrate preparation, adhesive or mortar, joints, skirting and wastage. Ask for samples in the actual lighting and confirm slip performance for bathrooms, balconies and external areas.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  13. How do I choose tiles for a small house?
    Published answer

    For a small home, choose tiles by room function, slip resistance, finish, size, grout layout, light reflection and maintenance—not by size alone. Larger tiles can reduce grout lines but may need a flatter substrate and careful cutting; smaller tiles can suit slopes and compact wet areas. Use slip-resistant surfaces in bathrooms and balconies, check shade and calibre consistency across boxes, and plan tile joints and skirting before installation. Buy an adequate quantity from the same batch and retain spare tiles for future repairs.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  14. What is the difference between M20 and M25 concrete?
    Published answer

    M20 and M25 are concrete strength grades, with the number representing the specified characteristic compressive strength in MPa at the standard testing age under the applicable specification. A higher grade is not automatically the correct choice for every member: mix design, exposure, durability, workability, member design and structural drawings determine the required concrete. Use the grade specified by the structural engineer and approved mix design; do not upgrade or downgrade at site without approval. Keep batch, delivery and cube-test records.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗BIS – IS 10262 concrete mix proportioning ↗
  15. Can I use ready-mix concrete for an individual house?
    Published answer

    Yes, ready-mix concrete can be used for an individual house when the mix is designed for the specified grade and exposure, the supplier is reliable, and delivery and placing can be managed properly. Confirm the approved mix design, delivery ticket, batch time, workability checks, sampling and cube testing plan, pump access and pour sequence. Do not add water at site without authorised direction because it can change the mix properties. Plan enough labour, vibration, finishing and curing before the truck arrives.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 4926 ready-mixed concrete ↗BIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  16. How do I calculate cement bags for house construction?
    Published answer

    Do not estimate cement bags for an entire house using a universal bags-per-square-foot thumb rule. Calculate concrete volumes from the structural drawings and use the approved mix design to determine cement content; calculate mortar and plaster separately using their specified proportions, thickness and measured areas. Add only a justified allowance for handling and wastage. For ready-mix concrete, cement is already included in the supplier’s designed mix. Ask the quantity surveyor or engineer to prepare a material take-off and reconcile purchases with actual work.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 10262 concrete mix proportioning ↗BIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  17. What is a bar bending schedule and why is it important?
    Published answer

    A bar bending schedule (BBS) is a reinforcement list prepared from the structural drawings. It identifies each bar mark, diameter, shape, cutting length, bends, quantity and location, helping the site team order, cut, bend and place steel correctly. It supports quantity checks and reduces avoidable waste, but it must match the latest approved drawings and detailing. Ask the engineer or authorised detailer to issue and revise the BBS when drawings change; never let a fabricator change bar lengths or laps independently.

    Official referencesBIS – IS 1786 reinforcement steel lookup ↗BIS – IS 456 reinforced concrete code ↗
  18. When should anti-termite treatment be done during construction?
    Published answer

    Anti-termite protection should be planned as part of the building design and construction specification, with treatment stages coordinated before they are concealed by flooring, backfill or other work. The exact method and timing depend on the approved product, site conditions, foundation details and manufacturer’s instructions. Use a qualified applicator, verify the product label and safety data, protect occupants and workers, and keep application records and warranty documents. Do not apply chemicals casually or assume one treatment eliminates all future termite risk.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  19. How do I prevent cracks between brick walls and RCC columns?
    Published answer

    Cracks at masonry-to-RCC junctions can result from different material movement, shrinkage, poor bonding, inadequate junction detailing or structural movement. Prevention starts with sound masonry workmanship, proper connection and detailing as specified by the designer, suitable curing and compatible plastering. Mesh or other reinforcement at junctions may be specified for some systems, but it is not a substitute for correcting movement or poor support. If a crack is wide, recurring, progressive or accompanied by distortion, have the structural engineer inspect it before cosmetic repair.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code ↗
  20. What should be included in a construction site inspection checklist?
    Published answer

    A useful site inspection checklist follows the construction sequence and records what will become hidden. Before foundation concrete, check setting-out, excavation dimensions, soil conditions, reinforcement, cover, formwork and any required engineer approval. Before each slab or beam pour, verify the latest drawings, bar sizes and spacing, laps, anchorage, cover, openings, embedded services, shuttering, props, concrete grade, testing and curing arrangements. During masonry and services, inspect line, level, junctions, conduits, pipe pressure tests and drainage falls. For waterproofing, record substrate preparation, corners, penetrations, membrane application and water-test results. At handover, close snags and collect approvals, test reports, warranties and as-built drawings. Record date, location, photos, responsible person, corrective action and sign-off for every inspection.

Permissions, legal checks & homeowner handover10 questions+
  1. How can I verify a building permission in Telangana?
    Published answer

    Use the official BuildNow portal to search or retrieve the permission using the application number and download the digitally issued proceedings and sanctioned plan. Check that the applicant, plot number, survey details, extent, address, floors, height, use and drawing revision match the property and the construction on site. Compare the approved plan with actual setbacks, parking and floor layout; a permission document alone does not prove that the building was executed in accordance with it. If the portal record is unclear, ask the competent local body or a licensed technical professional to verify it before purchase or construction.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗BuildNow – FAQs on downloading and verifying permissions ↗
  2. What is the difference between layout approval and building permission?
    Published answer

    Layout approval concerns how a larger parcel is divided and developed into plots, roads, open spaces and utilities. Building permission or the applicable registration route concerns the specific house or building proposed on an individual plot. An approved layout does not automatically approve every house design, floor count or setback on each plot. Before buying, check the layout approval and its conditions; before construction, separately verify the building approval route for the exact plot, proposed use, height and jurisdiction through BuildNow.

    Official referencesBuildNow – layout and building approval system ↗BuildNow – FAQs ↗
  3. Is an Encumbrance Certificate enough to verify a property title?
    Published answer

    No. An Encumbrance Certificate is an important search of registered transactions recorded for the specified property and period, but it is not a complete title guarantee. It may not reveal every unregistered claim, pending litigation, boundary dispute, inheritance issue, fraud, acquisition restriction or mismatch in survey details. Have an independent property lawyer examine the original sale deed and link documents, seller authority, revenue records, survey boundaries, land use, layout approval and relevant court or government restrictions. Match the records to the physical plot before paying an advance.

    Official referencesTelangana Registration and Stamps – official services ↗Bhu Bharati – land status ↗
  4. What happens if my house is built differently from the sanctioned plan?
    Published answer

    A deviation can lead to notices, penalties, refusal of completion or occupancy documentation, revocation of permission or enforcement action, depending on the nature and extent of the deviation and the applicable law. Do not assume that a small change is automatically permitted. Compare the work with the latest sanctioned drawing and ask the licensed architect or competent authority whether revised approval is required. Stop the affected work until the lawful route is clear; never conceal deviations or rely on an informal assurance that they will be regularised later.

    Official referencesBuildNow – FAQs on deviations and enforcement ↗BuildNow – government orders and rules ↗
  5. Can I change my house plan after building permission is approved?
    Published answer

    A design change after sanction may require a revised application or approval, especially if it affects setbacks, built-up area, height, floors, use, parking, structural members or other scrutinised parameters. Before executing the change, ask the licensed technical professional to compare it with the sanctioned plan and confirm the current BuildNow procedure with the competent authority. Keep the revised digitally approved drawing on site and give the structural engineer updated information where the structure is affected. Do not build the change first and assume that approval can be obtained afterwards.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval portal ↗BuildNow – government orders and rules ↗
  6. What is a road-widening line and how can it affect my plot?
    Published answer

    A road-widening line or proposed road alignment can reserve part of a property for future public road improvement. It may affect the usable plot area, building line, access, setbacks, compound wall and the feasibility of a proposed plan. Do not rely only on the existing road edge or a neighbour’s construction. Ask the architect or planning professional to check the current master plan, road alignment and any notified reservation for the exact survey number, and obtain written clarification from the competent authority before finalising the purchase or building footprint.

    Official referencesHMDA – planning information ↗BuildNow – land-use and approval portal ↗
  7. When should I hire a structural engineer for house construction?
    Published answer

    Engage the structural engineer before finalising the architectural plan and foundation, not only after excavation. The engineer should review the site and soil information, design the foundation and structural system, issue coordinated drawings and reinforcement details, and clarify changes during construction. Arrange inspections at key hold points such as foundation reinforcement, column and beam steel, slab pre-pour and any repair or alteration. Seek the engineer’s advice before removing walls, adding floors, cutting beams or slabs, changing material grades, or addressing significant cracks and honeycombing.

  8. What documents should I collect when my house construction is complete?

Obtain a signed handover and snag-closure list, plus the contractor’s written defect-reporting process. Keep digital and paper copies together; requirements vary by project category and local authority, so confirm the exact statutory documents for your building.

  9. What is a defect-liability period in house construction?
    Published answer

    A defect-liability period is the contractually defined time after a milestone or handover during which the contractor must respond to specified workmanship or construction defects, subject to the agreement. It is not a vague promise that “everything is covered.” The contract should state the start date, duration, covered defects, exclusions, response and repair timelines, access arrangements, emergency procedure and any separate manufacturer warranties. Record defects in writing with photos and dates, and retain the signed closure record. Have a lawyer review the clause before signing because obligations depend on the contract and applicable law.

    Official referencesBIS – National Building Code of India ↗
  10. How should I approve extra work and cost variations during construction?
    Published answer

    Use a written variation order before the extra work begins. It should describe the changed scope, drawing or location, quantities and measurement method, material and labour rates, taxes, total price impact, schedule impact and any effect on warranty or other work. Ask the contractor to attach supporting quotations or rate analysis and obtain approval from the person authorised under the contract. Update the BOQ, payment schedule and site records, and keep dated photos. Avoid verbal instructions and retrospective bills; unresolved variations are a common source of budget and completion disputes.

    Official referencesBuildNow – official approval and document checklist ↗
Foundation, services & homeowner project controls15 questions+
  1. How do I know whether my plot needs a soil test before construction?
    Published answer

    A soil investigation helps the structural engineer understand the ground conditions below the proposed house. It is especially important where the plot has filled soil, variable ground, nearby water bodies, slopes, previous excavation, signs of settlement or where the proposed structure and local requirements call for it. Ask a qualified geotechnical professional to recommend the investigation scope and issue a site-specific report. Do not select a foundation type or depth from a neighbour's building or a generic online chart.

  2. What does safe bearing capacity mean in a soil test report?
    Published answer

    Safe bearing capacity is a geotechnical design value used to assess the pressure that the ground can support under the assumptions and safety factors in the soil report. It is not a universal number for a neighbourhood: soil layers, groundwater, depth, settlement limits and test methods matter. Give the complete report to the structural engineer, who must check both bearing and settlement and design the foundation accordingly. Do not use a single value copied from another plot.

  3. Can I decide the footing size based on my neighbour's house?
    Published answer

    A neighbour's footing may sit on different soil, at a different depth, carry different loads or have been designed under different rules. Even adjacent plots can contain different fill, groundwater or soil layers. Foundation dimensions and reinforcement must be determined by a qualified structural engineer using the proposed building loads and suitable site investigation. Treat a neighbour's foundation only as background information, never as a design instruction.

  4. Why is a plinth beam provided in a house?
    Published answer

    A plinth beam is a structural member at or near plinth level that connects parts of the building's foundation or frame as designed. Depending on the structural system, it can help tie columns and support masonry or manage differential movement; its role is not identical in every building. Its dimensions, reinforcement, concrete grade and connection details must follow the structural drawings. Do not cut, omit or alter a plinth beam to accommodate plumbing or door openings without written engineering approval.

  5. How do I check terrace waterproofing before laying tiles?
    Published answer

    Before covering terrace waterproofing, check that the substrate is prepared, corners and upstands are detailed, pipe penetrations and rainwater outlets are sealed, and the designed slope drains water without ponding. Conduct the specified ponding or other system test for the required duration and record the result before laying protection or tiles. Confirm compatibility of the waterproofing, screed, adhesive and tile system. Protect the membrane from punctures during subsequent work and retain the product warranty and installation record.

  6. How should concrete be cured during hot weather in Telangana?
    Published answer

    Hot weather increases evaporation and can cause rapid moisture loss in fresh concrete. The site team should plan casting time, material temperature, transport, placement, finishing and immediate curing protection according to the approved mix and project specification. Use the specified curing method and duration; do not add water at the site or change the mix informally to improve workability. The engineer and concrete supplier should set the controls for the actual weather and member.

  7. Should I use AAC blocks or red clay bricks for my house?
    Published answer

    AAC blocks are generally lighter and larger than many conventional clay bricks, which can reduce dead load and speed up laying when the system is designed and installed correctly. Clay bricks have different availability, weight, thermal and moisture characteristics. Compare tested product properties, dimensional tolerance, water absorption, mortar or adhesive system, wall thickness, lintel details, service chasing and fixing methods. The structural designer must account for the chosen masonry system and its connections; workmanship and curing matter for either option.

  8. What is the correct plaster thickness for internal and external walls?
    Published answer

    There is no single plaster thickness that is correct for every wall. It depends on the masonry or concrete substrate, line and level, plaster system and project specification. Large thicknesses can crack or debond and may indicate that the underlying wall needs correction or a designed multi-coat system. Check surface preparation, mesh at dissimilar-material junctions where specified, curing, straightness and finished dimensions. Agree the approved thickness and method with the architect or site engineer before plastering.

  9. How do I choose exterior paint for a house in Hyderabad?
    Published answer

    Exterior paint selection should start with the wall substrate, local exposure, orientation, dampness and the manufacturer's technical data. Correct cracks, salt deposits and water ingress first; then use the specified primer and compatible coating system. Compare weathering performance, water-vapour behaviour, coverage, number of coats, warranty conditions and maintenance instructions rather than colour or brand name alone. Test a sample on the actual wall and ensure rainwater detailing prevents repeated wetting.

  10. What should I check before connecting my house to a sewer line?
    Published answer

    Before connecting to a public sewer, confirm that a connection is available and obtain any required approval from the responsible local authority or utility. A plumber should verify the connection level, pipe gradient, diameter, inspection chambers, venting, backflow risk and access for cleaning. Test the completed line for leaks and flow before covering it. Do not connect stormwater drains to a foul sewer unless the local authority expressly permits that arrangement.

  11. Is rainwater harvesting required for an individual house in Telangana?
    Published answer

    Rainwater-harvesting obligations can depend on the current state and local-body rules, plot size, building type, location and approval conditions. Check the latest requirement with the authority handling the building permission rather than relying on an old threshold or generic online statement. A workable system needs suitable roof catchment, first-flush arrangements where specified, filtration, safe recharge or storage design, overflow routing and maintenance access. Have the recharge design checked against site soil and groundwater conditions.

  12. What provisions should I make for rooftop solar during construction?
    Published answer

    If rooftop solar may be added later, ask the structural engineer to review the proposed panel and support loads and identify suitable mounting zones. Coordinate conduit routes, inverter and battery locations, ventilation, maintenance access, earthing and protection devices before ceilings and waterproofing are finished. Avoid drilling the completed terrace membrane without an approved detail. The electrical installer must verify current utility interconnection, metering and safety requirements before commissioning.

  13. What is a comfortable staircase riser and tread for a house?
    Published answer

    Staircase riser and tread dimensions must be consistent and comply with the building rules applicable to the project. Comfort also depends on total floor-to-floor height, number of steps, landing size, headroom, width, handrails, lighting and the needs of household members. Have the architect dimension the full stair section before construction and check the first and last risers against finished floor levels. Do not rely on a generic dimension that may not meet local requirements.

  14. What clauses should a house construction agreement include?
    Published answer

    A house construction agreement should identify the parties, site, approved drawings, detailed scope, BOQ or pricing basis, material and workmanship specifications, exclusions, start and completion milestones, payment schedule, measurement method, taxes, variation approval, site safety, utilities, inspection rights, delay handling, defects and warranty obligations. Attach the latest signed drawings and specifications and define how disputes and termination are handled. Have a qualified legal professional review the agreement before signing, especially for high-value work.

  15. How can I verify a contractor's stage-wise construction bill?
    Published answer

    Check a stage-wise bill against the signed BOQ, actual site measurements, approved drawings and the milestone definition in the agreement. Ask for measurement sheets, dated progress photographs, delivery records where relevant and written approval for every variation. Verify that quantities are not billed twice and that incomplete or defective work is treated according to the contract. Confirm taxes, prior payments, retention and deductions before releasing funds; avoid paying solely on a verbal progress estimate.

Construction planning, BOQ & project delivery4 questions+
  1. How do I plan a house construction project step by step?
    Published answer

    Plan the project in a deliberate sequence. First verify title, plot boundaries, access, land use and the applicable approval route with independent legal and technical professionals. Commission a site survey and, where advised, a geotechnical investigation. Develop an architectural brief around family needs, budget, future expansion, daylight, ventilation and parking; then coordinate architectural, structural, electrical, plumbing and other service drawings before pricing. Obtain the required permissions before starting work. Prepare a detailed BOQ and written specifications, compare contractor bids on the same scope, and sign an agreement defining milestones, quality checks, variations, delay treatment and defect obligations. During construction, record inspections and concealed services before they are covered, track costs and changes in writing, and test systems before handover. The exact sequence and approvals depend on the site and project category; use licensed local professionals.

  2. What should be included in a house construction BOQ?
    Published answer

    A BOQ (Bill of Quantities) should describe each work item clearly enough that two contractors price the same scope. Include item description, location, unit of measurement, estimated quantity, material specification and grade where relevant, workmanship or installation requirements, and the rate and amount. Break work into logical sections such as earthwork, concrete, reinforcement, masonry, plaster, waterproofing, flooring, doors/windows, electrical, plumbing and painting. State whether transport, loading, scaffolding, wastage, testing, taxes, debris removal and protection are included. Identify provisional quantities, owner-supplied items, exclusions and assumptions. Link important items to approved drawings and product submittals. During execution, measure completed work jointly and record approved variations separately. A BOQ is only useful when its descriptions and measurement rules are unambiguous; ask the designer or quantity surveyor to review it before signing.

  3. How do I prepare a construction schedule for a new house?
    Published answer

    Build the schedule from the approved scope and dependencies, not from an optimistic single completion date. Start with design, soil investigation, permissions and procurement decisions; then map site preparation, foundation, plinth, frame, masonry, services, waterproofing, finishes, testing and handover. Identify activities that cannot overlap safely—for example, concealed service testing must precede closing walls or floors. Include realistic lead times for steel, windows, tiles, joinery and specialist equipment, as well as inspection hold points, curing periods, weather and public holidays. Assign an owner to each activity and update planned versus actual progress weekly. Track decisions and materials that could delay the critical path. The contractor should provide a baseline schedule and explain revisions; do not shorten structural or product-specified curing and testing periods simply to recover time.

  4. What is the difference between carpet area, built-up area and super built-up area?
    Published answer

    Carpet area generally refers to the usable floor area within the internal walls of a home, subject to the definition used by the applicable regulation or agreement. Built-up area commonly adds wall thickness and certain covered spaces to the usable area. Super built-up area is a commercial term that may add a proportionate share of common areas in a larger development. These terms are not interchangeable, and the exact inclusions can vary by legal context and document. Ask for a dimensioned plan and a written area statement that explains balconies, terraces, shafts, walls and common areas separately. For a construction quotation, confirm whether the rate is based on plot area, plinth/built-up area, carpet area or another measured quantity. Compare projects only after aligning the measurement basis and scope.

Foundation, RCC & concrete quality6 questions+
  1. How do I select the right foundation for my house?
    Published answer

    The foundation must be selected by the structural engineer using the building loads and site-specific ground information. Relevant factors include soil strata and bearing characteristics, settlement risk, groundwater, nearby foundations, slope, fill, basement requirements and the number and arrangement of floors. A geotechnical investigation may be needed to inform the design; a neighbour's footing or a rule of thumb is not a safe substitute. The engineer then coordinates the foundation type, dimensions, reinforcement, founding level and construction sequence with the architectural layout and applicable standards. During excavation, the actual soil and groundwater conditions should be checked against the report, and unexpected conditions referred back to the engineer before concrete is placed. Do not alter footing depth, size or reinforcement on site without written design approval.

  2. What is the difference between isolated footing, combined footing and raft foundation?
    Published answer

    An isolated footing typically supports one column where soil and spacing conditions permit. A combined footing supports two or more columns, often where columns are close together or a boundary limits an individual footing. A raft or mat foundation spreads loads over a large area and may be considered where soil conditions, column layout or settlement considerations make it appropriate. These are broad descriptions, not selection rules: the correct system depends on geotechnical data, structural loads, settlement, groundwater, adjacent properties, construction feasibility and cost. The structural engineer should document the design assumptions and drawings. Never select a foundation by copying a nearby house or choosing the option that uses the least concrete; inappropriate foundations can cause serious movement and damage.

  3. What checks should be completed before a roof slab concrete pour?
    Published answer

    Before a roof slab pour, compare the work with the latest approved structural and service drawings. Check reinforcement bar size, spacing, laps, anchorage and support; cover blocks and chairs; openings and sleeves; electrical conduits and plumbing provisions; slab thickness and levels; and cleanliness of the formwork. Inspect shuttering, props, bracing, joints and safe access for leaks or movement. Confirm that concrete grade, mix documentation, quantity, delivery sequence, sampling and testing arrangements are ready. Ensure the engineer or authorised site supervisor has inspected and signed the pre-pour checklist. Photograph concealed work and record any approved changes. Do not pour over unresolved discrepancies or rely on a verbal assurance that a missing bar or service opening can be fixed later.

  4. How can I check reinforcement steel before slab casting?
    Published answer

    Check reinforcement against the approved structural drawings and bar-bending schedule, not against a generic online spacing chart. Verify bar diameter, number, spacing, direction, top and bottom layers, extra bars, crank or support details, lap positions and development/anchorage as specified. Confirm that reinforcement is clean enough for proper bond, tied securely and held at the required cover with suitable blocks and chairs; bricks or loose stones are not acceptable substitutes for specified cover supports. Check openings, sleeves and embedded items with the services drawings before concrete placement. Have the responsible engineer inspect and record the work. If a bar is missing, displaced or conflicts with a conduit, stop and obtain an approved correction rather than cutting or shifting reinforcement informally.

  5. What is a concrete slump test and why is it done?
    Published answer

    A concrete slump test is a field check of the consistency or workability of fresh concrete using a standard cone procedure. It helps the site team assess whether a delivered batch is within the specified workability range; it does not directly measure compressive strength or prove that concrete is durable. Sampling and testing should follow the applicable standard and project quality plan, with results recorded against the truck/batch, time and mix details. Workability can be affected by transport time, temperature and admixtures. Do not improve slump by casually adding water at site: any permitted adjustment must be authorised, controlled and recorded under the supplier's mix procedure and engineer's direction. Strength assessment requires the specified sampling and compressive-strength testing as well as proper placing, compaction and curing.

  6. Should water be added to a ready-m mix concrete truck at the construction site?
    Published answer

    Do not add water to a ready-mix truck simply because the concrete looks stiff or is difficult to place. Uncontrolled water changes the water-cement ratio and can reduce strength and durability, increase shrinkage and cause segregation or bleeding. If workability is outside the approved range, inform the supplier and responsible engineer. Any adjustment, if permitted by the approved mix design and applicable procedure, must be made by authorised personnel, measured, mixed adequately and documented; the resulting concrete may need retesting. Check delivery time, mix identification, slump requirements, temperature and site handling before discharge. The safest practice is to specify the correct mix and placing method in advance and ensure adequate labour, vibration equipment and access. Never conceal an unauthorised water addition in the pour record.

Flooring, waterproofing & finishes4 questions+
  1. How do I choose tiles for a house floor?
    Published answer

    Choose floor tiles by room use first, then appearance. For bathrooms, balconies and other wet areas, prioritise suitable slip resistance and water-related performance for the actual surface condition. For living areas, consider abrasion and impact resistance, furniture loads, cleaning, glare and how visible dust or scratches may be. Check tile size against room dimensions, falls and drain locations; large tiles can reduce grout joints but require a suitable substrate and skilled installation. Compare actual samples in the room's lighting and check shade, calibre, batch consistency, edge quality and recommended adhesive and grout. Confirm skirting, thresholds, movement joints and transitions between materials. Keep spare tiles from the same batch for future repairs and follow the manufacturer's installation instructions.

  2. What is the difference between vitrified, ceramic and porcelain tiles?
    Published answer

    Ceramic and vitrified/porcelain tiles are manufactured and classified differently, but marketing labels alone do not tell you whether a product suits a particular room. Compare the manufacturer's technical data for water absorption, breaking strength, abrasion or wear classification, stain resistance, surface finish and recommended application. Porcelain is generally a denser, lower-absorption ceramic category, while vitrified is a broad trade term used for products made through vitrification processes; terminology can vary by market. For wet floors, ask for tested slip-performance information relevant to the expected use, not just a glossy showroom appearance. Also check calibration, shade variation, rectification, adhesive compatibility and maintenance. Select by documented performance and installation requirements rather than assuming one label is always superior.

  3. How do I prevent bathroom leakage during house construction?
    Published answer

    Prevent bathroom leakage by treating waterproofing as a complete system, not just a coat of chemical on the floor. Prepare a sound, clean substrate and form the required falls to drains. Use a compatible waterproofing system with the specified primer, coats, reinforcement at corners and pipe penetrations, upturns and termination details. Coordinate floor traps, sleeves, thresholds and wall finishes so there are no gaps in the water barrier. Follow the product data sheet for application thickness, coverage, curing and protection. Conduct and document the specified ponding or water test before tiling, and inspect the ceiling or adjoining spaces below. Protect the membrane during tile work and use compatible adhesives and grouts. If leakage appears, identify the source before applying a surface patch that may hide the real defect.

  4. What is the correct slope for a bathroom floor and balcony?
    Published answer

    A bathroom or balcony floor should drain continuously toward its outlet without reverse falls or standing water. The required slope is determined by the design, floor dimensions, drain positions, finish material and applicable local requirements; there is no single slope figure that should be copied blindly into every project. Before tiling, check the screed levels with a straightedge and water test, confirm the drain is at the intended low point and ensure thresholds prevent water escaping into adjacent rooms. Large-format tiles may need careful cutting and setting around floor traps. Verify that waterproofing remains continuous at corners, doorways and pipe penetrations. A completed floor should be tested for ponding and drainage before handover, with any low spots corrected before fixtures and finishes make repair difficult.

Electrical, plumbing & building services3 questions+
  1. How do I plan electrical points before plastering?
    Published answer

    Plan electrical points from a furniture and appliance layout before conduits are installed. Mark beds, wardrobes, TV units, kitchen counters, work desks, refrigerators, washing machines, AC indoor/outdoor units and likely future equipment. Ask a licensed electrical professional to calculate connected loads, circuit distribution, protective devices, earthing and cable sizes in accordance with applicable rules. Locate switches and sockets for convenient access while considering children, water zones and furniture clearance. Plan dedicated circuits where required, adequate outlets, data/Wi-Fi points, doorbell, exhaust fans and outdoor lighting. Coordinate conduits with beams, columns, plumbing and false ceilings; never cut structural members to route wiring. Photograph conduit routes before plastering and keep an updated circuit schedule and as-built drawing for future maintenance.

  2. What should I check before concealed plumbing pipes are covered?
    Published answer

    Before concealing plumbing, inspect the pipe system against the approved layout and manufacturer's instructions. Confirm pipe material, diameter, pressure/temperature rating, route, supports, gradients for drainage, cleanouts, sleeves and isolation valves. Check that joints were made with the correct tools and compatible fittings, and that pipes are protected from sharp edges, sunlight where unsuitable, heat sources and movement. Pressure-test water-supply lines and test drainage lines using the specified method before closing chases or floors; record the results and rectify leaks. Keep access to valves, traps and serviceable connections. Photograph the completed routes with measurements from fixed reference points and retain product invoices and warranty details. Testing should be performed by a qualified plumber under the project quality plan.

  3. How do I choose UPVC, CPVC and PPR pipes for a house?
    Published answer

    UPVC, CPVC and PPR are different piping systems and should be selected for the service they are designed and certified to perform. UPVC is commonly used for certain cold-water, drainage or waste applications depending on the product system; CPVC is commonly used for hot and cold potable-water distribution; PPR is a thermoplastic pressure-pipe system joined by heat fusion. These general descriptions do not replace the manufacturer's ratings. Compare pressure class, temperature range, potable-water certification where relevant, UV exposure limits, chemical compatibility, joining method, fittings availability, installation skill and warranty. Do not mix incompatible brands or joining systems without written approval. Ask the plumber to provide product data and follow the exact system instructions, then pressure-test or leak-test the installation before concealment.

Ventilation, quality checks & handover3 questions+
  1. How do I plan ventilation and natural light in a new house?
    Published answer

    Good daylight and ventilation start with the room layout and site context. Study the sun path, neighbouring buildings, road noise, prevailing breezes, privacy and rain exposure before fixing window sizes and positions. Where possible, provide openings on more than one side of a space to support cross-ventilation, while ensuring airflow is not blocked by partitions or furniture. Use shading, overhangs, screens or suitable glazing to control glare and heat gain; more glass is not automatically better. Kitchens and bathrooms need effective exhaust or ventilation provisions. Coordinate window openings with lintels, beams, columns, waterproofing and security. A local architect should check the plan against plot setbacks, ventilation and building rules applicable to the site.

  2. What should I inspect during house construction before making stage payments?
    Published answer

    Before paying a construction milestone, compare the contractor's claim with the agreement, BOQ, approved drawings and actual completed work. Ask for joint measurements or inspection records for items that will soon be concealed, such as reinforcement, waterproofing and plumbing. Check material delivery evidence, test reports, quality observations and approved samples where relevant. Separate original contract work from written variations, and confirm the rate, quantity and time impact of each change before payment. Verify arithmetic, taxes, previous advances, retention and deductions against the contract. Do not pay solely because a calendar date has arrived if the milestone is incomplete, and do not withhold agreed payments without following the contract's process. Keep signed measurement sheets, bills, receipts and photographs in one project record.

  3. What should be checked during final house handover?
    Published answer

    Walk through the house systematically with the contractor and designer before final payment. Test each tap, flush, drain, water heater, pump and visible plumbing connection; check for leaks and adequate drainage. Test lights, switches, sockets, protective devices and the electrical panel with a qualified electrician. Operate doors, windows, locks, shutters, drawers, fans and appliances; inspect tile lippage, grout, paint, sealants, skirting, counters and visible cracks. Check roof and wet-area waterproofing records, external drainage, rainwater pipes and access covers. Prepare a snag list with room, defect, responsible party and target date, then re-inspect completed items. Collect approved/as-built drawings, permissions and completion documents where applicable, warranties, product manuals, test certificates, keys, spare tiles/paint and service contacts. Record meter readings and handover date in writing.

Weekly site supervision & pre-construction2 questions+
  1. What should I check at a house construction site every week?
    Published answer

    Walk the site on the same day each week and record dated photographs from repeatable viewpoints. Compare actual work with the approved drawings, BOQ and current schedule. Check the quality and storage of delivered materials, protection of completed work, housekeeping, access and basic site safety. Review inspection and test records for work completed or about to be concealed, such as reinforcement, plumbing and waterproofing. List defects with location, responsible person and due date; recheck old items before closing them. Record labour and material delays, decisions needed from the owner and any proposed variations. Ask the site engineer or contractor to sign the weekly record. This is a monitoring aid, not a substitute for inspections by qualified professionals.

  2. What should be checked before foundation excavation starts?
    Published answer

    Before excavation, confirm that the latest approved drawings, site survey, boundary information and setting-out dimensions are available. Have the surveyor or authorised professional establish and protect benchmarks and verify building lines, offsets and levels. Identify underground utilities, nearby foundations, access routes, spoil-storage areas and dewatering needs. Review the soil investigation and the engineer's excavation and shoring requirements. Put barriers, warning signs, safe access and a site-specific excavation safety plan in place; protect neighbouring property and public areas. Confirm who will inspect the exposed founding stratum and what to do if actual soil, water or obstructions differ from expectations. Do not deepen, widen or relocate an excavation without the engineer's written direction.

RCC inspection & workmanship3 questions+
  1. What should I inspect before footing reinforcement is covered with concrete?
    Published answer

    Before concrete placement, compare the footing excavation and reinforcement with the approved structural drawings and bar-bending schedule. Check footing dimensions and founding level; bar diameter, count, spacing, direction, laps and anchorage; column starter-bar location and projection; and specified concrete cover using suitable cover blocks and supports. Confirm reinforcement is tied securely, reasonably clean and not resting on soil. Check that formwork, if used, is stable and dimensions are correct; remove loose soil, standing water and debris as required by the method statement. Verify service sleeves or earthing provisions that must pass through the foundation. Have the responsible engineer inspect and record approval. If anything differs from the drawings, stop and obtain a documented correction rather than improvising at site.

  2. What should I check in formwork before an RCC beam or slab pour?
    Published answer

    Inspect formwork against the approved dimensions, levels and structural details before a beam or slab pour. Confirm shuttering is rigid, adequately supported, braced and founded on a stable base; props and connections must match the temporary-works plan and remain clear of movement or settlement. Check joints for grout leakage, soffit levels, beam depth, slab thickness, camber where specified, openings, edges and construction joints. Ensure the inside is clean and release agent is used correctly without contaminating reinforcement. Verify safe working platforms, access, guardrails and a clear concrete-discharge route. Check that reinforcement, cover, conduits and embedded items have been inspected too. A competent supervisor should sign the pre-pour checklist; do not remove props or alter supports without authorised instructions.

  3. What should I check after removing slab and beam formwork?
    Published answer

    After stripping formwork, inspect concrete systematically in good light. Look for exposed reinforcement, honeycombing, voids, cold joints, cracks, chipped edges, unusual surface variation, water leakage and signs of movement. Record locations and photographs before patching or plastering. Compare beam and slab levels and any visible deflection with the engineer's acceptance criteria; do not judge structural safety by appearance alone. Keep curing and protection in place as specified. Report significant cracks, deep voids, exposed bars, unexpected deflection or damaged members promptly to the structural engineer. Repairs should follow an approved method after the cause and extent are assessed. Never cover a suspected structural defect with mortar, plaster or paint to make the surface look finished.

Materials, finishes & homeowner selection4 questions+
  1. How do I compare AAC blocks and red clay bricks for a house?
    Published answer

    AAC blocks are generally lighter and larger than conventional clay bricks, which can reduce dead load and speed up walling when the system is correctly specified. Red clay bricks are familiar to many local teams and may be easier to source or repair in some areas. Compare the actual product's density, strength, dimensional tolerance, water absorption, thermal and acoustic performance, fire rating, availability and test documentation. The wall system also depends on mortar or adhesive, joint thickness, mesh at junctions, lintels, chasing methods, anchors and plaster compatibility. AAC requires suitable thin-bed adhesive and compatible detailing; ordinary brickwork practices may not transfer directly. Compare installed cost and workmanship availability—not just per-block price—and follow the structural and architectural specification.

  2. How do I compare cement brands and grades for house construction?
    Published answer

    Do not select cement on brand name or advertised strength alone. First confirm the cement type and grade specified by the structural designer for the intended work and the applicable Indian Standard and current product certification. At delivery, check sealed bags, manufacturer, batch or packing date, consistent labelling and signs of moisture damage or hard lumps. Store bags off the floor on a dry raised platform, protected from rain and damp walls, and use stock in a controlled first-in-first-out sequence. Keep different cement types and batches identifiable. For bulk or critical work, retain delivery records and arrange tests where required by the quality plan. Never change cement type or mix proportions at site without approval from the engineer or mix designer.

  3. How do I choose a kitchen countertop material for daily use?
    Published answer

    Choose a kitchen countertop by considering daily use, budget, appearance and the cabinet support beneath it. Granite is a natural stone with variation between slabs and may need periodic sealing depending on the variety and finish. Engineered quartz offers more consistent patterns but can be sensitive to high direct heat and some chemicals; follow the manufacturer's care limits. Other options, such as solid surfaces or stainless steel, have different repair, heat, scratch and hygiene characteristics. Compare sample slabs in the actual kitchen light, inspect seams and edge details, and confirm cut-outs, sink support, overhangs, wall upstands and joint sealing. Ask for written information on thickness, substrate support, installation, stain care and warranty. Always use trivets and follow the selected product's maintenance instructions.

  4. How do I choose bathroom tiles that are safe and easy to maintain?
    Published answer

    For bathroom floors, prioritise a tile with documented slip performance suitable for wet barefoot use; a glossy surface may look premium but can become slippery. Choose wall tiles for water exposure, cleaning chemicals, soap deposits and grout maintenance. Check tile size against floor falls and drain positions, because large formats may need careful cuts to avoid ponding. Review shade, calibre, batch, surface texture, edge quality and adhesive compatibility from physical samples. Select grout and sealant as part of the system and confirm movement joints where needed. Ask the installer to demonstrate drainage and inspect the completed waterproofing test before tiles cover it. Keep spare tiles and the product details for future repairs.

MEP, waterproofing & handover3 questions+
  1. What should a homeowner check before approving electrical wiring?
    Published answer

    Before approving wiring, compare the point layout with the furniture and appliance plan and the latest electrical drawings. Confirm that the licensed electrician has designed circuit grouping, cable sizes, load balance, protective devices and earthing for the actual loads and applicable code. Check conduit routes, bend radii, junction-box access, separation from plumbing and coordination with beams and ceilings. Verify dedicated supplies where specified for heavy appliances, AC, pumps and water heaters. Confirm the distribution-board schedule and labels, socket and switch locations, weather protection outdoors and appropriate protection in wet areas. Before energising, obtain the required insulation-resistance, polarity, continuity and earthing test records from a qualified professional. Never accept a visual check as proof that an electrical installation is safe.

  2. What should I check before approving a waterproofing contractor's work?
    Published answer

    Ask the contractor to identify the exact waterproofing product/system, approved substrate preparation, primer, number of coats, coverage or thickness, reinforcement at corners and pipe penetrations, upturns and termination details. Confirm that drains, thresholds, sleeves and wall-floor junctions are included—not just the open floor area. Check batch numbers, expiry dates, application conditions and the manufacturer's instructions. Ensure each layer is allowed to cure and is protected from damage by following trades. Before tiling, require a documented ponding or other specified water test for the required duration and inspect adjoining rooms or ceilings below. The written warranty should state the covered areas, exclusions, duration, maintenance obligations and response process. A product warranty does not replace correct design and workmanship.

  3. What should a house construction handover snag list include?
    Published answer

    Create one snag-list line per defect and include room, exact location, description, dated photo, severity, responsible trade, target completion date and closure evidence. Cover walls and ceilings, paint, tile alignment and grout, skirting, counters, sealants, doors, windows, locks, wardrobes, hinges and drawer operation. Test every tap, flush, floor trap, water heater, pump, drain and visible pipe connection. Test lights, switches, sockets and protective devices with a qualified electrician. Check balcony and terrace drainage, waterproofing test records, external rainwater pipes, access panels and safety items such as railings. Record missing documents, warranties, manuals, keys and spare materials separately. Re-inspect repairs and mark an item closed only when the result is verified. Attach the final signed snag list to the handover record.
